headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure from Chatwoot outputs feeding Whisper, while Whisper itself has no write or network capabilities.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages, reports, and integrations, so its outputs may contain attacker-controlled text. Whisper has no clipboard, MCP, or filesystem ingestion, so the direct bridge is weak; however, if an operator pipes Chatwoot text into Whisper workflows, prompt-like content could be misread as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is manually copied into a downstream text-processing prompt or transcript pipeline
IF Whisper is wrapped by an orchestrator that treats transcribed text as instructions
mitigations: Use a fixed delimiter around Chatwoot text before transcription
Strip markup and role-like tokens from Chatwoot exports
Review any Whisper wrapper prompt for instruction-following language
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to Chatwoot-derived text
requires-engineering: block instruction execution on transcribed customer content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, but Whisper has no network egress, no filesystem read, and no API calls. The pair does not show a default path for Whisper to exfiltrate Chatwoot data; leakage would require an external operator to move data between them. That makes the blast radius limited and the pathway non-default.
conditions: IF an operator exports Chatwoot customer records into audio or text files for Whisper processing
IF a separate wrapper copies Whisper transcripts back into Chatwoot without redaction
mitigations: Avoid sending customer records to Whisper unless redacted
Keep Whisper offline and isolated from Chatwoot exports
Delete temporary transcription files after use
requires-engineering: add DLP checks before export
requires-engineering: segregate customer-data workflows from speech workflows

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but Whisper has no filesystem write, no git modification, no subprocesses, and no network egress. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict between the pair is not plausible from the documented capabilities.
conditions: IF Whisper is embedded in an external system that adds write or network permissions not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep Whisper in read-only batch mode
Do not grant Whisper filesystem write access
Do not co-locate both agents on a shared mutable workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks if future write paths are introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate customer-facing messages, reports, and integration outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. Whisper produces transcriptions, and if those transcripts are fed into Chatwoot workflows without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect support actions or replies. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are imported into Chatwoot macros, tickets, or automations without human review
IF Chatwoot actions are triggered from Whisper output as if it were ground truth
mitigations: Require human review before using Whisper transcripts in Chatwoot
Mark Whisper output as untrusted in the workflow
Limit Chatwoot automations on transcript-derived fields
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before actioning transcripts
requires-engineering: log transcript provenance in support tickets

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Whisper handles audio and speech. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, and Whisper has no network egress or file access that would independently widen compliance exposure. Any compliance issue would come from operator-controlled data movement rather than the pair itself.
conditions: IF customer audio or transcripts are routed from Chatwoot into Whisper under a policy that forbids that data class
IF retention settings differ between Chatwoot exports and Whisper-derived artifacts
mitigations: Confirm which customer data classes may be transcribed
Delete Whisper artifacts on a short retention schedule
Redact personal data before transcription
requires-engineering: document residency and retention for transcript storage
requires-engineering: add policy checks before export
